# The decision behind the third amendment to criterion 3

**Asked, on 25 September 2026, after the ninth review at note 129.** Record 121
stopped the implementer's copies varying by slice, and that removed the routed
model and effort from the Codex agent TOML as well as the Claude Code copy, so
nothing now carries a route to a Codex implementer; three places still say the
TOML does. The cost that decision was offered named only the Claude Code effort,
and as built it is both keys on both assistants. Which way?

**The options put to him, in the order they were offered.**

1. Say the effort is carried and not applied on both: amend criterion 3 a third
   time to state that the routed model reaches the implementer through the spawn
   instruction on both assistants and the routed effort is recorded and reported
   rather than applied on either, and fix the spawn text, the generator docstring
   and the amendment to match. Keeps the copies stateless, which is what stopped
   the ticket merging; costs the effort being applied anywhere until a later
   ticket can carry it. Marked as the recommendation.
2. Put the route back into the Codex TOML alone, leaving the Claude Code copy
   fixed. Delivers criterion 3's Codex half as amended and reintroduces a
   generated file whose content depends on which slice is in hand, on one
   assistant, which is the state-dependence behind four findings and the blocked
   merge.
3. Give the spawn instruction the whole job on both, with neither generated file
   carrying a route. Honest and uniform, and it rests entirely on a Codex
   mechanism no session has ever exercised on this repository, so it would ship
   unverified.

**What he chose.** Option 1.

**What it settles, and what it admits.** The route decides the model and the
effort, and the model is what reaches the work: through the per-invocation
override in Claude Code and through the spawn instruction in Codex. The effort
is decided, recorded, carried in the pack, written into kpi.json and read by
SEEN-109, and applied by nothing. That is less than the ticket's description
promised and it is what was built; the criterion says so rather than the code
being described as if it did more.

**Why the alternative was refused rather than deferred.** Option 2 would have
delivered the letter of the amendment by putting a ticket's state back into a
generated file, on one assistant. That file was wrong on a detached HEAD, after
a replan, the moment a green landed and after the receipt, and it is why this
ticket could not merge. Delivering a criterion by rebuilding the thing that
blocked delivery is not delivering it.
